refutation_attempt: Ran a case-fold collision scan over all 11114 paths of commit 009d40f5 (git ls-tree): zero file collisions, one directory case pair (cmake/Tests, cmake/tests). Checked every CMake consumer of both spellings resolves by exact case on a case-sensitive tree.
reason: cmake/Tests holds ModuleProbes and the *Case scripts; cmake/tests holds the webgpu_*.cmake scripts and linker-selection-probe. No file name occurs in both, so a case-insensitive checkout merges them losslessly, and each -P/-S reference (UnitTests.cmake, ModuleProbes.cmake, webgpu examples CMakeLists) names the existing case. Hygiene, not a defect.

entry.title: HeadlessPlatform::InjectEvent, the display-free event seam, has no caller and no test
entry.summary: HeadlessPlatform::InjectEvent is documented as the way to test input, runtime and lifecycle behaviour with no display, yet nothing calls it and no test covers inject-then-PollEvents delivery; the only refill test drives a test-local FakePlatform.
entry.expected: PLAT-115 is marked done with the acceptance that tests can push PlatformEvents into the queue, which is described as what lets input, runtime and lifecycle behaviour be tested with no display server, and the InjectEvent header comment calls it the mechanism that makes those behaviours testable. A seam with that role should have at least one test that injects events into a HeadlessPlatform and reads them back through PollEvents, in order, then finds the queue empty.
entry.actual: At 009d40f5 InjectEvent appears only in its declaration in the private header modules/platform/src/Headless/HeadlessPlatform.hpp, its one-line definition in HeadlessPlatform.cpp and the PLAT-115 plan row. PlatformConformance runs against Headless but only checks that PollEvents clears a stale batch, is safe on an empty queue and keeps capacity. IPlatformTests checks clear-and-refill on FakePlatform, a test-local class that reimplements the queue, so a regression in HeadlessPlatform's own queue would go unseen. Input tests call PlatformInputBridge::ProcessEvent directly. InjectEvent is not on IPlatform, so code outside the platform module cannot reach it through a public header. The CnaPlatformTests filter names a HeadlessPlatform* token that no suite matches, and no test suite named for the class has ever existed.

entry.evidence: Read the files named and searched modules, tools, tests, cmake and docs at 009d40f5 for InjectEvent and for HeadlessPlatform test suites; searched history up to the target for a TEST(HeadlessPlatform...) suite and found none. Nothing was built or executed.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a stated per-OS support matrix or an offered combination that configures but cannot build. PlatformSelection.cmake defines the offered set as host and detection driven and refuses reserved names loudly; the X11 detector says Unix-like hosts, which includes macOS with XQuartz.
reason: The rule is stated in the files themselves: the available list is built from host conditions and installed dependencies, reserved identifiers fail configure, and nothing in CNA promises that every offered name is validated on every OS. The candidate observes the design, not a broken contract; related evidence gaps are published as CNA-VGAP-011 and CNA-VGAP-012.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a contract that forbids side effects in GetCapabilities or requires every SDL_InitSubSystem to be paired, and for a production SDL_Quit that would make the process-static latch stale. IPlatform allows process-lifetime pinning; camera is not a PlatformSubsystem; no production code calls SDL_Quit.
reason: Deliberate and explained in Sdl3Camera.cpp (BINDFIX-020): SDL_GetCameras returns nothing until SDL_INIT_CAMERA runs and camera ids die with the session, so the subsystem is started once and never quit. The contract only says capabilities are read once and permits pinned subsystems. The missing test for this path is already published as CNA-VGAP-007.

refutation_attempt: Searched every Terminal source for a writer to queued_; only the declaration and the append-and-clear in PollEvents mention it. Checked that PollEvents still clears the caller's batch first and fills it from the input decoder and resize watcher.
reason: queued_ is a dead member: PollEvents appends and clears an always-empty vector. Delivery, ordering and the clear-first contract are unaffected because resize and input events come from the watcher and decoder. Cosmetic leftover with no observable effect.

refutation_attempt: Looked for any caller of SetComposeSuppressed and for a duplicated-text path. None calls it; EmitText also requires an active text input, and AnInputMethodComposesKoreanAndCommitsIt asserts nothing is typed while composing and only the syllable after commit.
reason: The setter is dead and its header comment describes wiring that does not exist, but no defect is observable: EmitText is gated on active text input, and on the tested Mutter plus ibus stack the input method consumes its keys and the suite pins the no-duplicate result. That suite runs only by hand, which CNA-VGAP-012 already records.

refutation_attempt: Enumerated every platform's Show*FileDialog for a PlatformException thrown after the callback is taken: SDL3 and Win32 only for an empty callback, X11 and Wayland only without a portal, which their capability already reports as false. No reachable throw drops a real callback.
reason: The catch-and-drop in FileDialog is unreachable with the shipped platforms: the capability gate answers unavailable through ReportUnavailable, portal failures arrive as an empty result, and MessageBox::Show's -1 is documented. It would matter only for a future platform that throws after accepting the callback, contrary to the header's wording.

refutation_attempt: Checked whether an empty callback leaves a continuation pending or a dialog open: RequireCallback and Win32Dialogs refuse before showing anything, and IPlatformDialogs documents the callback as must not be empty. Nothing was registered, so nothing waits.
reason: The platform contract requires a non-empty callback and refuses before any dialog opens; FileDialog swallowing that refusal leaves a caller who supplied no continuation exactly as it asked. At most an undocumented no-op for a meaningless call.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a path where TryAcquireFrame returns true while the state is not Ready, and for a producer of CameraState::Closed. Sdl3Camera and the canned camera both return false unless Ready, and no code path yields Closed.
reason: Camera.hpp's promise (false when not Ready) is met one layer down: the platform contract says false while not ready and the only real provider checks GetState. Closed is an unused enumerator with no Close method, which harms no caller and is already recorded on the site's internals page.

refutation_attempt: Followed a platform change through EnsureService and ReleaseService: the old Haptic reference is dropped without ReleaseSubsystem because the old platform is no longer installed. Checked that Sdl3Platform's destructor releases exactly its owned counts and deactivates haptics, so the imbalance ends with that platform.
reason: Not calling into a possibly destroyed, uninstalled platform is the deliberate trade in ReleaseService. The leftover Haptic reference lives only as long as the old platform object, whose destructor releases what it acquired, and production code installs one platform per process.

refutation_attempt: Compared NativeDiagnosticSink::Record with its header, NEXTdevices.md and DEVPERF-005's resolution for any promise of release-build logging. All three say logging is debug-only and the counter, last record and callback are test hooks.
reason: The implementation matches its documented policy: debug builds log through the CNA logger, every build counts and stores the last record, and the observers are named ForTesting. Whether release builds should log is a design choice recorded in the plan, not a contract breach.

refutation_attempt: Checked that the synchronous canned callback is stated in the header and that asynchronous timing is pinned somewhere real: the X11 and Wayland portal suites assert the answer arrives only from the pump. Win32's early callback is CNA-BUG-182.
reason: The synchronous callback is a documented test simplification, not a claim about real platforms, and the asynchronous contract is tested at the platform layer for the portal services. The real violation, Win32 calling back inside Show, is published as CNA-BUG-182, and canned-only devices tests are CNA-VGAP-007 and CNA-VGAP-037.

refutation_attempt: Traced an omitted Shutdown to process exit: the atexit fallback is registered after the singleton's constructor completes, so it runs first; ReleaseService calls the captured platform only if still installed, and CurrentPlatform state is immortal. Found no call into a destroyed platform.
reason: Shutdown is documented as an application obligation with the atexit fallback as the safety net; the backend destructor skips release after the flag and otherwise checks platform identity. The out-of-process ordering harness is spawned by a registered gtest. Its exclusion from the devices workflow filters is already published as CNA-BUG-035.

refutation_attempt: Read the Known gap section and all four sensor Dispose implementations, looking for a stronger promise about same-instance Dispose against Start. The doc cites the WP7 floor (instance members not thread safe); Compass and Motion no longer have the described shape.
reason: A Dispose racing Start on one instance is documented as an unsupported usage, matching the XNA and WP7 baseline that instance members are not guaranteed thread safe. refutation_attempt: Tested the premise that events never replay against the decompiled XNA 4.0 SignedInGamer IL (its SignedIn add accessor invokes the new handler per signed-in gamer) and GamerServicesDispatcher.Update. Looked for a CNA replay hook on SignedIn; only NetworkSession has one.
reason: The premise is false for XNA 4.0: SignedIn is raised from Update and replays every already signed-in gamer to a new subscriber. CNA's plain event is raised inside Initialize and never replayed, so handlers added afterwards miss the four stub gamers and the CNA demo works around it. CNA replays GamerJoined this way but not SignedIn.

entry.title: SignedInGamer::SignedIn does not replay already signed-in gamers to a late subscriber, unlike XNA 4.0
entry.summary: XNA 4.0 raises SignedIn during Update and its add accessor replays each already signed-in gamer to a new handler; CNA raises it inside Initialize on a plain event, so a handler added afterwards never hears about the four stub gamers.
entry.expected: In the genuine XNA 4.0 GamerServices assembly (read from its decompiled IL), sign-in changes are raised from GamerServicesDispatcher.Update, and SignedInGamer.SignedIn has a custom add accessor: after combining the delegate it loops over Gamer.SignedInGamers and invokes the newly added handler once for every gamer already signed in. The XNA documentation likewise says the event is raised during calls to Update. A game can therefore subscribe at any time and still learn who is signed in. CNA already reproduces such a replay for NetworkSession::GamerJoined, through an EventHandler replay hook, and docs/c-api/NET.md documents that behaviour.
entry.actual: SignedInGamer::SignedIn in SignedInGamer.cpp is a plain System::EventHandler with no replay hook, and GamerServicesDispatcher::Update is empty. Initialize raises OnSignIn once for each of its four stub gamers, synchronously inside the call, and a handler added afterwards is never called for them; the game must read Gamer::getSignedInGamersProperty() instead. The CNA presence demo subscribes 'before Initialize() runs so every SignedIn firing during startup is observed', and the C route cna_signed_in_gamer_subscribe_signed_in_ext adds its handler the same way. SignedOut is never raised in production, because OnSignOut has no caller outside SignedInGamerTestAccess. SignedInGamerTest.SignedInEventFires raises the event only after subscribing, so no test pins late-subscriber behaviour.

The SignedInGamer header cites FNA's plain event declaration as its model, and CLAUDE.md says matching FNA is no defence for a behaviour XNA does not have. Nothing was built or executed.

Drains occur at construction, Invoke, Run entry and exit, and Dispose.
reason: A binding design choice at cna-cs e223909, forced by CNA's documented handle thread affinity (a finalizer-thread release is refused). Where the binding drains is its own policy; CNA behaves as documented, so there is no CNA defect at TARGET.

refutation_attempt: Read cna-java's NativeBindings and bindings.json at the pinned revision: COMPILED_ABI_VERSION is 0.21.0 and the recorded rationale cites CNA's own 0.x rule. Refusing 0.29.0 follows from that; looked for a CNA promise that would make it a CNA defect and found none.
reason: External repository fact verified at cna-java 6661173: compiled ABI 0.21.0, admission requires the same major and minor, and the rationale quotes ABI_VERSIONING.md. Refusing TARGET's 0.29.0 is the binding behaving as designed. The site's C API page and Java internals page already say so.

refutation_attempt: Confirmed at the pinned revision that cna-java's README says ABI 0.20.0 and 1,225 routes while NativeBindings and bindings.json say 0.21.0. Searched CNA text for any repeated claim; none.

refutation_attempt: Read NativeDeferredRelease.java at the pinned revision: its own javadoc states the trade (a Cleaner only queues, the owning thread drains on the next framework pump, a thread that never pumps again leaks). Looked for a CNA rule it violates; CNA refuses off-thread release.
reason: A binding design within CNA's documented thread-affinity contract, stated candidly in the class's own javadoc at cna-java 6661173. The limitation belongs to the binding, and CNA at TARGET behaves as documented.

refutation_attempt: Compared cna-python's Renderer enum at the pinned revision with TARGET's published renderer constants: 14 values (7, 23 to 30, 32, 34, 35, 39, 49) are retired at TARGET. Checked that graphics.h documents their refusal and MapRendererType returns InvalidArgument for them.
reason: CNA behaves exactly as graphics.h documents: retired values and values above CNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERER_MAXIMUM are refused by every route that takes a renderer identity. The stale members are migration debt in cna-python f085bbb, not a CNA defect.

refutation_attempt: Confirmed the route exists at TARGET in the header, the implementation and the ABI baseline exports, and that cna-python's PENDING_ROUTES at the pinned revision still lists it as exported by no measured artifact.
reason: A stale entry in an external repository, measured against older artifacts: cna_network_session_replace_session_properties is declared in net_sessions.h, implemented in CnaCApiNetSessions.cpp and recorded in abi_baseline.json at TARGET. Nothing is missing in CNA.

refutation_attempt: Read TryBeginFrame, FinishFrame and FrameScope against Game::Tick's frame scope, and searched docs and the C API for an application-driven BeginFrame contract. Found none: the frame is process-wide by definition, and an application BeginFrame inside a tick is refused and counted.
reason: The frame is one process-wide engine frame; a nested application BeginFrame is refused and counted in malformedFrameCount, and an application EndFrame ends the engine frame early. That is misuse of an API whose documentation says engine frame, surfaced by the malformed counter, and no C route exposes it. A documentation sentence would help.

refutation_attempt: Read vendored enet_peer_send, enet_deinitialize, the backend's Send callers, discovery registration and the NetworkSession Begin* guards. Drops occur only for unconnected peers, invalid channels or oversize packets; the channel limit of two matches the channels used; only one session can register.
reason: ENet refuses only when the peer is not connected, the channel is invalid or the packet exceeds the host maximum, so nothing deliverable is lost. enet_deinitialize is empty on Unix and only timer and Winsock cleanup on Windows, which exit supersedes. Discovery keeps one registered session, matching the enforced one-active-session rule.
read: third_party/enet/unix.c and win32.c::enet_deinitialize (git show at the target)
